about.text: Fermented camel milk made by camel herders in the pastoral areas of Sudan. Traditionally it ferments while the herd is on the move: the jolting of the camel's walk shakes the milk in its bag. Herders start each batch with soured product kept back from earlier batches instead of a pure culture.

how.label: ferment in skin bags
how.text: Sudanese gariss ferments in large skin bags that keep a stock of soured product, shaken as the nomads travel. Streptococcus infantarius and L. fermentum make the acid, and Kluyveromyces marxianus yeasts make some alcohol.
